classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish nonzero turning points, which remain stationary, from a zero turning point, which becomes a vertical asymptote.

inlines.text: How many stationary points are there on

spec.description: Both ends rise. The left minimum touches the x-axis at x=-1; the curve crosses the y-axis at 2, reaches a maximum between 2 and 3, then has a positive minimum below 1 before rising again. No grid or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Qualitative supplied graph with three stationary points, exactly one of them on the x-axis. Bézier positions reproduce the schematic relationships; no equation or additional numerical values are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; contains no reciprocal answer.

answer.worked: The two stationary points with nonzero ordinates remain stationary points after taking reciprocals; their maximum/minimum roles reverse. The stationary point at $(-1,0)$ becomes a vertical asymptote, so it is not a stationary point of the reciprocal graph.
